message.content:
In a standard poker game the “most hearts” a single player can hold is limited by the number of cards that make up their hand.

| Game | Cards per player | Max hearts a player can hold |
|------|------------------|------------------------------|
| 5‑card draw (or 5‑card stud) | 5 | **5 hearts** (a 5‑card flush) |
| Texas Hold’em (or Omaha) | 7 (2 hole + 5 community) | **7 hearts** (a 7‑card flush) |

So, in Texas Hold’em the highest possible number of hearts a player can have is **seven**—all seven cards being hearts. That would be a royal flush of hearts (A‑K‑Q‑J‑10‑9‑8 of hearts, for example). In a 5‑card hand the maximum is five hearts, which would also be a flush.

**Bottom line:** The player who can have the most hearts is the one who holds a 7‑card flush of hearts in Texas Hold’em (or a 5‑card flush in a 5‑card game).
